title: Standard SKU key and duplicate check
objective: Build a standard SKU key such as SNE-450-42 from a category name, a style number and a size, then flag duplicate keys.
instructions: The standard SKU key is: the first three letters of the category in capitals, a hyphen, the style number padded to three digits with leading zeros, a hyphen and the size (for example SNE-450-42, or SAN-045-38 for style 45). In D2:D7, build the key from columns A, B and C. Clean the category with TRIM first, use LEFT for the three letters and UPPER for capitals, and pad the style number with RIGHT("000"&B2,3). In E2:E7, show Duplicate when the same key appears more than once in D2:D7 and Unique when it does not, using IF and COUNTIF. Fix the key range with $ signs.
hints: Build the key in parts and join them with &. Part 1: UPPER(LEFT(TRIM(A2),3)). Part 2: RIGHT("000"&B2,3). Part 3: C2. Put "-" between them.
To pad the style number, join 000 in front and keep the last three characters: RIGHT("000"&B2,3) turns 45 into 045 and 450 into 450 (the zeros in front are cut off).

COUNTIF(range, value) counts how many cells in the range equal the value. Each key counts itself once, so a key that is unique has a count of 1. Test for more than one: =IF(COUNTIF($D$2:$D$7,D2)>1,"Duplicate","Unique").
